study.title: CDKD-w+: A Keyframe Recognition Method for Coronary Digital Subtraction Angiography Video Sequence Based on w+ Space Encoding

imaging.modality_detail: Coronary DSA image sequences (grayscale, resized to 512x512) from multiple C-arm positions
imaging.frames_per_sequence: each sequence contains at least one complete heartbeat cycle; 959 images over 50 sequences

public_dataset_used.detail: Coronary DSA stenosis detection dataset by Danilov et al. (Sci Rep 2021), 100 patients

data_released.detail: Data availability statement refers to the source public dataset; release of the authors' keyframe labels is not stated

task.task_description: Heartbeat keyframe recognition (maximal vasodilation/vasoconstriction frames) in coronary DSA sequences by encoding frames into StyleGAN2 w+ space with a pSp encoder, computing inter-frame cosine similarity matrix, local minimum search and non-minimum suppression.
task.clinical_application: Selecting cardiac-phase-matched frames to aid 3D modeling/reconstruction of coronary arteries

temporal_evidence.quote: Differential analysis of inter-frame latent codes is employed for heartbeat keyframe localization

method.pretraining: Pre-trained EG3D network used to provide w+ latent labels for training the pSp encoder

G1.quote: Since there is currently no coronary DSA dataset serving the heartbeat keyframe recognition task

G3.quote: do not consider the impact of heartbeat on DSA images. This article fills this gap and achieves the localization of heartbeat keyframes

G4.quote: the 2D images may sometimes lack sufficient information, necessitating the construction of a 3D model

other_limitations: Only measures size of differences between paired frames; cannot directly distinguish vasoconstriction from vasodilation frames
future_work: Use a three-dimensional encoder for high-dimensional encoding to enable image difference detection without special labeling
Introduce image segmentation to independently locate vasoconstriction and vasodilation frames
